cards.b: The reasons why employees want to work hard and work effectively for the business.
High productivity, low absenteeism, low labour turnover, good ideas and cooperation, few disputes.
The rate at which employees leave a business and need to be replaced.
Mainly money. Break jobs into simple tasks and pay by piece rate. Ignores social needs; work becomes boring.
Physiological, security/safety, social, esteem, self-actualisation. A met need no longer motivates; the next level does.
Pay, working conditions, policy, supervision, job security. They prevent dissatisfaction but do not motivate by themselves.
Achievement, recognition, responsibility, interesting work, promotion. They create job satisfaction. Used through job enrichment.
Taylor: money is the main motivator. Herzberg: pay is only a hygiene factor.
A payment for each unit produced. Encourages output but quality may fall and pay is insecure.
Payment as a percentage of the value of sales made, often on top of basic salary. Suits sales staff.
Bonus: lump sum for hitting a target. Profit sharing: a proportion of company profit paid to employees.
Non-financial extras on top of pay, e.g. company car, health insurance, discounts, pension.
Rotation: swap between tasks at the same level. Enlargement: extra tasks of a similar level added to the job.
Adding tasks needing more skill and responsibility. Meets Herzberg's motivators and Maslow's esteem needs.

cards.f: Best reward for a small business with little cash
cards.b: Non-financial methods: praise, teamworking, responsibility. They cost little.

short.q: Explain why high labour turnover is a problem for a business. [2]
short.model: Many staff leave and must be replaced, which raises recruitment and training costs and can lower productivity.

short.q: Calculate the total pay of a worker on a basic salary of €1,200 plus 5% commission on sales of €30,000. [2]
Explain one limitation of Taylor's theory of motivation. [2]
short.model: It ignores social and esteem needs, so repetitive piece-rate work can become boring and quality may suffer as workers rush.
points: boredom or poor quality as a result

short.q: Explain the difference between job enlargement and job enrichment. [3]
short.model: Enlargement adds extra tasks of a similar level, giving variety. Enrichment adds more challenging tasks and responsibility, using more of the worker's skills.

short.q: A nurse and a factory worker both work at one hospital supplier. Explain why piece rate suits one but not the other. [4]
short.model: Piece rate suits the factory worker because output can be counted. It does not suit a nurse because output is hard to measure and quality of care matters more than speed.
points: quality could suffer under piece rate
